title: DigCompEdu Check-In | Build one digital judgment into each assignment

qcReview.basis: Publisher’s English supplement dated 2 June 2023, © Ersoy et al., CC BY 4.0, was verified against the preserved SHA-256. The 5 prompts, 25 ordered options and item weights match the registered area; scoring follows the publication’s 0–4 option order. This independent report uses the project’s complete-response area sum (0–20); the original study reports 22-item total levels and did not validate independent area use. No source grading bands are imported.

interpretations.headline: Build one digital judgment into each assignment
interpretations.summary:
A student group finds a persuasive online claim for a health education project. Before including it in a draft, they track the claim to its source, discuss what the evidence supports, and make a short resource for a test audience. As they revise it, they also decide which images and information they have a right to share.

Your answers describe opportunities you provide for learners to check information, communicate and collaborate, produce content, work responsibly online and solve concrete problems. A higher total reflects reporting more developed opportunities across these areas. It does not grade students’ digital skills. The report can help you choose a decision learners could practise within an existing assignment.

guidance.text: Use a fictional case or teaching claim. Ask groups to locate the original source, justify what they will include, make a small audience-facing artefact, and improve it after your feedback.

After the task, have learners explain one choice they made about reliability, collaboration or responsible sharing. They can show how they solved an access or format problem without sharing any real individual’s data.

limitations: Ersoy, H., et al. (2024). Digital competence of faculty members in health sciences measured via self-reflection: current status and contextual aspects. PeerJ, 12, e18456. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.18456 ; Supplemental Information 1, Digital Competency Assessment Questionnaire for Academicians, 2 June 2023 (https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.18456/supp-1). Used under CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Framework: Redecker, C. (2017), edited by Y. Punie, European Commission JRC, doi:10.2760/159770. This area-only presentation and feedback are project adaptations and imply no author or Commission endorsement.

This English reflection applies to adult higher-education faculty in health sciences. The original study used a convenience sample of 306 faculty members from six partner universities. The standalone area has no separate validation or local norms.

The area sum adds 5 equally weighted 0–4 items. Zero is a valid response; an omitted answer leaves the area result unavailable. No scale-wide total, A1–C2 level, percentile or individual certification is reported.
report.disclaimer: For your own professional learning in health-sciences higher education. This report describes self-reported digital teaching practice and supplies no basis for evaluating teaching performance, ranking faculty, or certifying competence.
